To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SCAMP provides reliable group membership management for gossip protocols in very large-scale systems.
SCAMP achieves the following properties: (a) It is fully decentralized and self-organizing, i.e., it does not require any centralized component or a global view.

(1) a peer-to-peer membership service can be provided in a fully decentralized fashion and (2) this service is scalable, i.e., the size of the view of each group member converges automatically to the size required by the gossip protocol to provide reliability guarantees.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new class of gossip-based protocols that are selforganizing and provide reliable communication in large groups with no global knowledge.
the development of a fully decentralized, scalable, and self-organizing membership protocol for large-scale groups.
the problem of how a fully decentralized peer-to-peer membership management protocol can be used to support a gossip-based communication protocol in a reliable way.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed protocol is a promising solution to the problem of scalable and reliable group membership management in large-scale groups.
SCAMP is the first fully decentralized gossip-based membership protocol that is scalable to very large-scale group sizes.
the SCAMP protocol is an efficient, scalable, and reliable membership protocol which can be used in conjunction with gossip-based algorithms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we present a fully decentralized membership management protocol that achieves reliability comparable to previous protocols based on global knowledge, and does so with much less overhead.
SCAMP provides a fully decentralized, scalable, and self-organizing membership protocol which is able to support gossip-based algorithms reliably.
SCAMP provides the same reliability as previous schemes based on a global view, but at much lower communication and computation overhead.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a fully decentralized membership protocol can provide reliable gossiping with a very small overhead.
a decentralized gossip algorithm can achieve the reliability of its centralized counterparts without the need for global knowledge of the group membership.
a fully distributed membership management protocol can provide similar reliability guarantees as protocols that require global knowledge.
